reviewer: Claude Code (AI assistant). Not an independent human review.
method: A sweep of every page of the year for passages shared word for word by 4 or more papers that no counted opening of round one explains; each passage read, looked up in the year's lists and counted by its own opening words against every page in both transcriptions, by the thin-year rule (Y-THIN as amended on 23 November 2026: items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted; single paragraphs from runs of news counted by their own words, C-09); the items printed by every surviving paper admitted at the owner's word of 25 November 2026; scan checks of each admitted passage
scan_scope: Each crop covers the excerpt, the opening of the printed item. Long documents were not proofread in full.

new_groups.label: London, July 1773: a letter from on board the Lord Camden East-Indiaman: 'As we left the Cape of Good Hope, we met two Dutch men of war bringing in a pirate'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a paragraph of the London news of July 1773 on a letter from on board the Lord Camden East-Indiaman, lately arrived from China: 'As we left the Cape of Good Hope, we met two Dutch men of war bringing in a pirate, which proved to be the Aurora English frigate, with part of her crew, who had murdered the Captain and all the officers, and ran away with the ship.' A London report of a letter from a ship, as the papers reprinted it; the New-Hampshire Gazette introduces the letter in other words (C-02).
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1773 printings, checked against the scan (round two: printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, found by the sweep check of 24-25 November 2026 and admitted at the owner's word).

dispositions_summary.method: Round two of 1773. The sweep check of 24 and 25 November 2026 (X-THIN-SWEEP; outputs/story_discovery_1779/sweep_check_25nov.md) read every passage of the 1773 pages shared word for word by 4 or more papers that no counted opening of round one explains, looked each up in the year's lists and counted it by its own opening words against every page of the year in both transcriptions. It found one item printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, which round one's lists did not name; asked, the owner chose on 25 November 2026 to admit it as the rule reads. Every printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/round2.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md; verdicts in scan_verdicts/round2*.json).
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: As in round one (Y-THIN as amended, B1): an item printed by every newspaper that survives for its weeks is admitted. The letter from the Lord Camden is printed by all 4 papers of its weeks.

counted_item_by_item.The letter from the Lord Camden: 4 of the 4 papers that survive for its weeks (MS 2 September, NHG 3 September, VG1 and VG2 9 September), counted by its own opening; the New-Hampshire Gazette introduces the same letter in its own words ('A letter from on board the Lord Cambden East Indiaman ... says'), counted with the others (C-02).
